answer: Each submission carries a per-key watermark derived from its private key, so copied wording still traces back to one operator. When the opal vault review finds two identities with near-identical output, the younger clone is flagged and its 22,000 POA bond burns, a third paid to the finder. A vine of clones thus costs one full bond plus genuinely original work per fake identity, scaling linearly, while an onyx-registered honest node submits once and loses nothing.
